Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Solara Renewables Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please refrain from using your telephone keypad during the call to minimize background noise. As a further reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Solara Renewables Inc.'s results for the Q3 2024 quarter. Joining me on today's call are Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Marcus Hale, Chief Financial Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Development Officer; and Sophia Grant, Chief Sustainability Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena Vasquez.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Solara Renewables Inc. had a strong Q3, reflecting our commitment to innovation and sustainability in the renewable energy sector. We continue to see increasing demand for our clean energy solutions and are well-positioned to capitalize on the growing market opportunities.

We want to highlight five crucial aspects of this quarter's achievements. First, on PPA pricing trends and contract extensions, we've seen stabilization and modest upticks in fixed-price tariffs, executing significant new agreements and extensions that bolster our revenue visibility. Second, storage deployment and hybrid project updates show accelerating progress, with key projects reaching milestones and hybrids dominating our pipeline. Third, debt levels and financing costs remain disciplined, with deleveraging and cost reductions strengthening our balance sheet. Fourth, the impact of government incentives and subsidies has been profound, driving cash flows and margins across regions. And fifth, construction progress and commercial operation dates are advancing steadily, with major projects on track or ahead of schedule.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Marcus Hale to provide a detailed overview of our financial performance.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Elena. We are pleased with our financial results for the Q3. Revenue reached $850 million, representing a 28% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by the successful commissioning of several new projects and higher energy production. Our gross margin improved to 42%, reflecting our efforts to optimize operational efficiency and manage costs effectively. Operating expenses totaled $210 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and expansion into new markets. Net income was $145 million, or $0.92 per share. We maintained a strong balance sheet with $1.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our financial outlook for the remainder of the year remains positive.

Let me expand on some of those key aspects Elena mentioned, starting with PPA pricing trends and contract extensions, which form the bedrock of our revenue visibility for our 12.5 GW portfolio of utility-scale solar, wind, and hybrid battery projects across North America and select APAC markets. In Q3, we executed 1.2 GW of new PPAs and extensions, up 25% quarter-over-quarter, at an average all-in pricing of $32 per MWh, showcasing our disciplined approach in a dynamic market.

PPA pricing has stabilized with a modest uptick over the past 12 months, reversing prior downward pressures. Our benchmarking against LevelTen Energy's PPA Price Index and NREL's Annual Technology Baseline shows U.S. national average for utility-scale solar PPAs at $29 per MWh in Q3 2024, up 8% year-over-year from $26.80 per MWh. Wind PPAs averaged $31 per MWh, a 6% YoY rise, while hybrid solar-plus-storage deals, now 40% of our new pipeline, fetched $38 per MWh—a 30% premium over pure solar—due to dispatchable value in grids like CAISO and ERCOT.

Regionally, ERCOT saw merchant prices average $55 per MWh amid summer heat and data center growth, allowing new solar PPAs at $35-42 per MWh for 15-year terms, with batteries pushing to $50 per MWh—a 15% premium reflecting our 2.5 GW interconnection-ready projects. In PJM, solar prices eased to $24 per MWh, down 2% YoY from oversupply and FERC Order 2023 delays. CAISO hybrids hit $45 per MWh, aided by LCFS credits of $8-12 per MWh.

Internationally, our 800 MW Australian assets gained from LGC spot prices at AUD 35 per MWh, up 12% YoY, supporting PPAs at AUD 55 per MWh equivalent. In Europe, German solar PPAs reached €28 per MWh or $30 USD, up 10%, via EEG reforms and TSO compensation.

Drivers include supply-demand balance: solar modules at $0.28 per Wdc post-IRA 45X, down 70% from 2022, but BOS costs up 12% from tracker delays and wage rules. Rates at 5.5% for tax equity compressed IRRs to 7.5%, requiring higher PPA floors for 1.8x DSCR. Tech like n-type TOPCon at 23.5% efficiency, bifacial gains, and 4-hour BESS at 90% RTE justify 20-25% uplifts per Aurora models.

On extensions, we've secured 1.8 GW YTD on 8 GW expiring by 2027—65% above guidance—at $34 per MWh blended, up 22% from legacy $28 per MWh. Examples: 450 MW Rattlesnake Solar in Arizona extended with APS at $37 per MWh, with dynamic clauses; 300 MW Wind Horizon in Oklahoma with OG&E at $36 per MWh, adding 200 MWh Fluence BESS for $5 per MWh ancillaries.

We're pursuing 'extension-plus' with VPPAs for 20-30% output, like 500 MW with Google/Microsoft at $40 per MWh equivalents, yielding 10-15% better economics. Index-linked escalators (CPI +1.5%) cover 70% of new deals.

Forward, our 15 GW pipeline has 6 GW PPA'd at $33 per MWh average, with 2 GW negotiating for Q4. Prices should firm 5-7% into 2025 per BNEF, with data centers adding needs. We've derisked with 4 GW PTOs and 85% domestic content for $15 per MWh PTC/X.

Next, debt levels and financing costs. Total gross debt at September 30 stood at $4.8 billion, down 8% YoY from repayments and cash flow from 8.2 GW operating assets. Net debt was $3.7 billion, at 2.8x net debt-to-EBITDA—within 2.5-3.5x target, better than peers.

Debt mix: 65% or $3.1 billion long-term non-recourse project finance (BBB+ rated) on assets like 500 MW Gemini Solar+Storage and 300 MW Hornsea Three. 25% or $1.2 billion corporate, including undrawn $750M RCF. 10% short-term bridges.

WAIR improved to 4.1%, down 120 bps YoY. Wins: $1.2B green bonds at 3.75%, upsized with SPT linkage; refi $600M at SOFR+140 bps. Interest expense $48M, 18% of EBITDA. 70% hedged, duration 7.2 years.

U.S. IRA PTC/ITC transferability cut costs 80-100 bps, e.g., $350M credits. Europe: €250M Innovation Fund for Poland wind at sub-3%. APAC: 1.8% JPY bonds for India JV.

Deleveraging via $800M asset sales, yieldco IPO, $2B EMTN. Capex $2.1-2.3B funded, ROIC 8-10%.

Finally, government incentives and subsidies contributed $187M in Q3 cash flows, 22% of EBITDA, up from 18% YoY, lifting FCF 14% to $312M. Globally, they drove $1.2T investments, cutting our LCOE to $28/MWh.

U.S. IRA: $122M or 65%, with 50% ITC on 1.2 GW SunForge ($450M credits at 95% monetized). BESS ITC on 850 MWh IronPeak ($68M).

Europe: €92M from EEG/SDE++, CfD AR6 at £42/MWh, PERTE grants for 5 GW fab.

APAC: RMB 1.2B China grants, India PLI for 2.8 GW, ASEAN JETPs.

Trends: PTC-like 45X ($52M, $0.07/Wdc cells), 48C R&D. 55/25/20 geographic mix hedges risks.

Projections: $750-850M 2025 FCF add.

Now, I'll pass the call to Jordan to discuss our project development pipeline.

Jordan Lee:
Thank you, Marcus. Our project development pipeline continues to grow, with 15 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making significant progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, which will further contribute to our revenue growth and profitability. We are also exploring opportunities to expand our project portfolio through strategic acquisitions and partnerships.

Building on Elena's highlights, let's cover storage deployment and hybrid updates, plus construction progress. Storage is key for firm clean energy, with hybrids at mid-60% EBITDA margins.

Q3 first energy: 450 MW/900 MWh across three projects, total operational BESS 2.3 GW/4.8 GWh YTD, up 180% YoY via CATL LFP integration, LCOS under $120/kWh. Utilization 75%, ancillaries 40% revenues.

Regionally: 300 MW/600 MWh Hornsdale expansion in Australia full ops; 150 MW/300 MWh ERCOT BESS earning $15M annualized arbitrage. 1.2 GW/2.4 GWh under construction (80% contracted), 800 MW/1.6 GWh Q4.

Hybrids 65% of 12 GW pipeline: 500 MW CAISO solar+storage NTP, 20-year PG&E PPA $55/MWh; 400 MW UK wind+storage FID at £49.50/MWh; 600 MW Texas PV+storage groundbreaking, Q2 2025 COD.

LDES pilot with Form iron-air; VPP 200 MW stacking. 2025: 4 GW deployments (60% hybrid), 5 GW pipeline 70% conversion.

On construction: 2.8 GW under construction, 1.7 GW COD 2025. Solar 55%: 650 MW Phoenix AZ 78% complete, first 150 MW energized, Q4 COD $28/MWh PPA; 400 MW Lone Star TX 62%, Q1 2025 phased.

Wind: 300 MW Atlantic Breeze offshore 45%, Q3 2025 first power. Storage: 500 MW/2 GWh Cascade CA 72%, Q4 COD.

U.S. 85%, Europe 250 MW Iberian H2 2025, India 150 MW 55%. 68% weighted complete, $2.1B capex. Vertical EPC 40%, favorable supply trends.

Next, Sophia will provide an update on our sustainability initiatives.

Sophia Grant:
Thank you, Jordan. Sustainability is at the core of our business, and we are committed to reducing our environmental footprint and contributing to a cleaner, more sustainable future. We have made significant progress in reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that promote sustainability. We believe that our sustainability efforts not only benefit the environment but also create long-term value for our stakeholders.

I'll now turn the call back to Elena for closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sophia. In conclusion, we are very pleased with our performance this quarter. We are confident that our strategic initiatives and our commitment to innovation and sustainability will drive continued growth and success in the years to come.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to register a question, please press star, then one on your telephone keypad. You will hear a tone acknowledging your request. If you are using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. As a reminder, please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Our first question comes from Sarah Chen with Greenlight Capital. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen:
Can you discuss the impact of supply chain constraints on your project timelines?

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Sarah. Supply chain constraints remain a watch item, but we've derisked significantly through vertical integration and multi-sourcing. For instance, module prices stabilized at $0.28/Wdc with IRA incentives, though BOS like racking saw 12% YoY rises from ILUC and wage compliance. We've shortened lead times with Tier 1 partners like LONGi/Trina and in-house EPC handling 40% of builds, cutting costs 8-10%. Weather like Hurricane Beryl hit Lone Star briefly, but modular systems recovered it. Overall, no material delays—Phoenix at 78%, Cascade 72%—with 5-10% buffers. Interconnection reforms like FERC 2023 affect PJM queues, but our 4 GW PTOs insulate us. We're on track for 1.7 GW CODs next year.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with EcoInvest Partners. Please go ahead.

Mike Patel:
What is your strategy for expanding into emerging markets?

Elena Vasquez:
Great question, Mike. Emerging markets are a high-growth priority, targeting 20-25% of capex by 2026. APAC is key: India PLI drove 2.8 GW backlog with Adani JV at 14% IRRs; Vietnam/Indonesia JETPs fund 500 MWh BESS. We're leveraging subsidies like China's Golden Sun for tandem cells and yen bonds at 1.8%. Strategy: JVs for local content (85% domestic), policy diversification (CfD, SDE++), and hybrids for grid stability amid coal phaseouts. Risks like FX hedged via swaps. This balances our 55% U.S./25% EMEA mix, chasing 20% CAGR.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with RenewTech Advisors. Please go ahead.

Lisa Wong:
How are you managing the increasing competition in the renewable energy sector?

Elena Vasquez:
Lisa, competition is intensifying, but our edges shine: 12.5 GW portfolio with 90% revenue locked to 2028, hybrids at 62% margins vs. 45% pure renewables, and fortress balance sheet at 2.8x leverage. Differentiation via tech—TOPCon bifacial, LDES pilots, AI optimizers—and backlog: 6 GW PPA'd at $33/MWh premiums. We're asset-light scaling: yieldco drops, $2B EMTN, no dilution. Policy positioning (IRA domestic content, EU Net Zero Act) and VPPAs with hyperscalers lock premiums. De-risked execution (68% construction complete) outpaces peers amid queues/delays.

Operator:
Thank you. There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Elena Vasquez for any closing remarks.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of Solara Renewables Inc. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
